subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through the vehicle design as a static model without needing a joint rig, since it's not a creature—just parts attached at root positions. Planning dimensions: a six-wheel carrier roughly 10 meters long, 3 meters wide, with wheel radius around 0.7 meters.

Now I'm laying out specific geometry: axle positions for three wheel pairs, a chassis frame box, a front cab, and the hull deck. I'm placing a rotating turntable toward the rear for a railgun mount, with a long elevated barrel built from paired rail boxes angled around 10 degrees so it extends forward over the cab.

Working out the wheel cylinders now, setting their radius, width, and rotation axis so they sit correctly under the chassis.

Adding hub decals and tread detail, then designing the four stabiliser legs with horizontal beams extending outward, diagonal hydraulic struts, and circular ground pads sized to bear the vehicle's weight.

For textures I'm planning camo mottling for the hull, hazard stripes, unit emblem and warning decals, glowing cab glass, and energy-coil style glow effects for the rails and lights, pulling in a glow kit for the lighting elements.

Now I'm sketching out helper functions for boxes and cylinders with position/rotation options, then listing the build order: chassis frame with rails and crossmembers, fender skirts over the wheel pairs, a cab with sloped windshield, roof, headlights, grille, exhaust stacks and mirrors, and finally the rear hull deck as a chamfered main body.

For the hull and cab I'm defining extruded side-profile outlines instead of simple boxes, using polygon points along the z-y plane to get the sloped silhouette shape, then giving the hull a camo paint job and sizing the cab to sit above the front axle.

Checking the wheel positions and widths against the cab to avoid intersections, then I'm adding fender/wheel-arch boxes outside the hull to cover the wheels, plus side skirt armor plates. For the turret, I'm placing a ring cylinder on top of the hull as the base for the turret body.

Now I'm working out the railgun geometry: computing a tilted direction vector for an 8° elevation angle, positioning twin rectangular rails along that direction from the trunnion pivot point, and verifying the muzzle end clears the cab roof.

Adding insulator clamps and glowing coil strips...

Still placing capacitor cylinders and glowing cable sweeps...

Now I'm positioning the barrel-aligned boxes so they stay correctly oriented along the tilt axis, then laying out the stabilizer beams, wheel axle spacing, and wheel occupancy ranges for the undercarriage.

I'm also sizing the piston assembly—outer and inner cylinder radii and heights, plus the pad cylinder dimensions and its slight sink into the base.

I'm adding a lathed pad with a chamfer, a diagonal brace rod connecting the hull bottom to the piston, and ground plates at the base. For the wheel treads, I'm weighing whether to add individual tread blocks around each tire's circumference, but worried that doing twelve per wheel across six wheels would push the part count too high, so I'm considering trimming to fewer tread blocks per wheel to stay within budget.

Still computing wheel geometry...

Now I'm adding the axle cylinders connecting the wheels, a differential pumpkin sphere, and small suspension arm details, then moving to the cab with a tinted windshield decal and sloped front profile.

Still placing windows and panels...

Adding roof hatches, antenna, radar dish on a mast, and twin exhaust stacks behind the cab, then working on the front bumper with hazard stripes, tow hooks, warm headlights, and red taillights at the rear.

I'm placing hull-side emblem decals with a star and "RG-06" text, figuring out the hull thickness and face positions, then starting to lay out the turret's side profile and pivot point.

Since the rails pass through the turret body near its trunnion, I'm reconsidering the turret shape—maybe splitting it into separate side cheeks with a gap for the rails, or just lowering the body so it sits below the rail line to avoid the overlap.

Now I'm shaping the cheek outlines and adding a breech housing box at the rear to tie them together, then checking that the rail geometry clears the body top as it extends from z=-1.2 to 6.2 — the clearance at the rear looks tight but acceptable.

Next I'm positioning the rails inside the cheeks, adding mounting blocks, and dividing the barrel shroud into painted dark-steel sections with cyan glow strips and orange hazard accents, plus clamp-style cover plates with ribs over parts of the rail run. Then I shift to placing the capacitor bank on the rear deck, working out its position relative to the hull top and turret center.

Working out capacitor placement and glow rings...

I should add a hatch and light bar, plus side tool boxes, jerry cans, ladder rungs, and antennas for detail. I'm planning the texture set — hub, glass, decal emblems with readable orientation, hazard stripes, warning labels, a radar screen display, and camo/tire paint — keeping it around six textures with a mottled olive camo and subtle countershading.

Writing camo paint function...

I'm deciding to add explicit joints for chassis, turret, barrel, and legs rather than relying on nearest-joint auto-assignment, since that could misattribute parts incorrectly. Since I'm not posing anything, I just need the rest pose to be structurally correct with each part bound to the right bone.

Deciding roles for wheels and legs, then setting up the imports and color palette with olive, dark, tan, and steel gunmetal tones for the vehicle's materials.

Now I'm building the camo paint functions mixing olive and dark with mottled patches, adding tan speckling based on noise thresholds, and a dusty tint near the bottom with lightening toward the top before starting the builder config.

Working through the wheel assembly: setting axle positions front/middle/rear on both sides, defining joints with mirrored directions, and laying out the tire, rim, hub, and decal parts with their respective colors and offsets.

Now I'm adding tread blocks arranged radially around the tire using rotation math to place each block at the correct angle, then starting on the mudguard geometry.

Positioning the mudguard panels and side skirts...

Still working out wheel-to-hull clearances and planning the chassis frame rails with steel material.

I'm checking placement for the decal and emblem against the mudguard positions, settling on the emblem near the rear hull side and leaving a free gap between the middle and rear mudguards for a number plate.

I considered adding a warning decal and tool boxes on the side hull but they clash with the mudguards and decal placement, so I'm skipping the boxes and fuel tanks for now and moving to defining the flat deck top spanning most of the hull length.

For the cab, I'm extruding the shape with 2.3 thickness. Then I'm adding a light bar on the roof, a sensor mast, and a lathed radar dish shape tilted up and forward using a custom axis direction.

Adding stabilizers now, with hydraulic pistons and a hazard-stripe paint texture on the pad using yellow-and-black stripes, bones connecting the beam, brace, outer cylinder, piston, and pad, and a beam box positioned along the stabilizer arm.

Working out piston and pad dimensions...

I'm positioning the turret ring, body, and barrel pivot now, checking that the ring cylinder aligns with the hull top and that the turret body's z-range stays centered correctly before sizing the cheeks.

Adjusting cheek positions to avoid overlapping the body width, then working out trunnion placement so the cylinders connecting the cheeks don't collide with the rails -- shifting them to stubs just outside the rail zone and adding cradle blocks around the rails for support.

I'm setting up a helper function to position gun parts along the barrel direction with perpendicular offsets, using a pitch-adjusted up vector, then defining the rails as a frustum box running from the breech to the muzzle with tapered width and height.

Now I'm detailing the glowing cyan accent strips running along the rail, plus periodic alternating black/steel bands and coil modules spaced along the barrel's length.

Adding coil capacitor boxes flanking the rails, then placing a darker muzzle brake with a glow ring at the barrel's tip, and a thicker breech cap behind the rails near the turret rear.

Switching to cab details now: a front grille texture with slats, glowing headlight boxes, a hazard-striped bumper, side mirrors, a door handle, roof visor, and rear tail lights with a tow hitch and striped rear bumper, plus small exhaust stack cylinders flanking the cab.

I'm checking that the stacks sit correctly against the sloped hull top near the cab, adjusting their base height and length so they clear the hull outline, then adding whip antennas tilted off the rear corners and planning hatch cylinders for the deck.

Then I'm adding vents, rear cooling radiators, capacitor pipes, a camera pod with a glowing screen texture on the turret cheek, an optics dome lens on top, and a rear ladder, estimating the total part count lands around 230, and wiring in bezier cable sweeps between the capacitors.

Now I'm sketching out the texture SVGs: a hub design with bolt rings and a yellow accent, a windshield glass texture with diagonal highlights and a wiper line, and a side window texture with rounded glass.

Then I'm adding an emblem SVG with a star inside a circle, "RG-6" text, and a stripe over a dark olive background, a warning label with yellow/black styling and a lightning bolt, and a radar-style screen with green grid lines and a sweeping blip glow. I'm starting a grille texture next.

Writing textured bumper parts...

Defining joint hierarchy next...

Continuing the hull outline points and checking the width matches the cab, then reusing the same camo paint pattern for both hull and cab for visual consistency. I'm working out the windshield's slope geometry, computing the normal vector for the angled hood and windshield segments to get lighting right.

Now I'm setting up the side windows based on the cab profile width at that height, then placing headlight boxes near the front corners with small box dimensions.

For the grille I'm sizing it against the front face height and width, keeping it centered between the headlights. I'm also defining tire shading with a mixed rubber color that adds a dusty mottled texture near the bottom using noise, and I'm double-checking that array types for point coordinates are correct before finalizing the cable sweep geometry with its start and end caps.

Checking capacitor placement and cable routing...
